claim_scope: The five rows are newly closed in this local investigation, not asserted newly resolved in the mathematical literature.

primary_reads.source: Ateniese, Blundo, De Santis, Stinson (1996), Visual Cryptography for General Access Structures
primary_reads.sections_read: Definitions2.1/2.2; Section5.3 Lemmas5.7-5.11; Example5.6; Section9 opening and table discussion
primary_reads.comparison: Collection versus basis distinction and unavoidable-pattern arguments are classical. Section9 explicitly treats strong structures on at most four participants. Example5.6 separates collections from basis for a WEAK structure and explicitly warns that the same construction does not reconstruct for the strong upward closure. It is not evidence against the present finite strong-structure result. No five-case priority conclusion follows from this source.

primary_reads.source: Shyu and Chen (2015), Minimizing Pixel Expansion in Visual Cryptographic Scheme for General Access Structures
primary_reads.observed: Crossref publisher-deposited title/authors/volume25 issue9 pp1557-1561 and references read. IEEE landing returned an AWS JavaScript WAF challenge. Publisher-deposited PDF returned HTTP418. No full-text theorem or table was read.
primary_reads.comparison: The original-model definitions, all five cases, lower bounds, and any overlap with the cone identity remain UNVERIFIED. No novelty claim is made.

primary_reads.source: Bose and Mukerjee (2010), Optimal (k,n) visual cryptographic schemes for general k
primary_reads.extent: Primary publisher abstract and references actually read; full text subscription-only.
primary_reads.comparison: The abstract concerns threshold access structures, Kronecker algebra, L1/LP characterizations and selected contrast-optimal threshold constructions. It does not state the five nonthreshold arbitrary-collection exclusions proved here. This is not an exhaustive nonexistence or novelty argument.

primary_reads.source: Tzeng and Hu (2002), A New Approach for Visual Cryptography
primary_reads.comparison: It explicitly changes reconstruction so the revealed image may be darker OR lighter than its background. Its reported expansion improvements cannot be imported into the fixed always-darker OR model without further model comparison.

primary_reads.source: Arumugam, Lakshmanan and Nagar (online2012; print2014), On (k,n)*-visual cryptography scheme
primary_reads.extent: Publisher abstract and deposited Crossref metadata actually read; publisher PDF endpoint redirected to subscription preview. No detailed numerical theorem or proof was obtained.
primary_reads.comparison: The primary abstract defines the strong structure with every minimal qualified k-set containing participant1. This is exactly cone((k-1)-out-of-(n-1)), including the fifth finite row as (3,5)*. The access family is therefore prior art. Whether its detailed collection bounds already give m=8 or the present general all-Gamma basis identity remains UNVERIFIED; no novelty claim is made.

discovery_only.observed: Index reports closed access, no OA URL and no repository full text. This is a discovery aid, not primary proof evidence.

unresolved_prior_art_obligation: Obtain lawful full text of Shyu-Chen2015, its cited 2013 experimental study, and Arumugam-Lakshmanan-Nagar2014, then compare the precise collection model and numerical bounds for these five access structures. Do not describe local closure as a new published-theorem improvement before that comparison.
